subject: chemistry
title: Signs of a Reaction
welcome_lead: Bubbles, sparks, smells, colours: nature shouts when chemistry is happening.
meta_desc: Spot signs of chemical reactions in this KS3 chemistry adventure on bubbles, colour change and heat.
final_note: You can now detect a reaction with your eyes, ears and nose.

concepts.def: Bubbles or fizzing show a gas is forming.
A clear shift in colour suggests a reaction.
The mixture gets hotter or cooler.
A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings.
A reaction that absorbs heat from surroundings.
A solid that forms when two liquids react.

walkthroughs.h2: Five clues to spot a reaction
walkthroughs.body_html: Watch for these signs: a gas bubbles off, a colour change, a temperature change, a solid appears in liquids (precipitate), or a new smell.

If the test tube gets hot, the reaction is exothermic (heat is given out). If it gets cold, it is endothermic (heat is taken in).

Burning is exothermic.

Bicarbonate of soda + vinegar = bubbles of carbon dioxide gas.

Rusting iron = a slow colour change from grey to red-brown.

A burning candle = light, heat and new substances (CO₂ and water).

Ice melting
Temperature change

options: Endothermic
Exothermic

Photothermic

mcqs.q: What is the role of the fingerprint region (below ~1500 cm^-1) in IR spectroscopy?
options: The fingerprint region is used to identify which functional groups are present.
It is unique to each compound — used to identify a specific molecule by matching to a known spectrum.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.
If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
